cards.explanation: The answer is My warriors. Verse 3 says, "I have commanded My sanctified ones; I have even summoned My warriors…" So the warriors are the ones summoned, friends, right alongside the sanctified ones.

The answer is wrath. The warriors are summoned "…to execute My wrath and exult in My triumph." That's a heavy word, so I'll just say it plainly: this burden is serious. Keep that word in your pocket, friends, because it keeps coming back in this passage.

The answer is the LORD of Hosts raising an army. Verse 4 says, "The LORD of Hosts is mobilizing an army for war." So all that noise on the mountains has one source. Quite a crowd, friends. My bakery has never once been that loud, and I include the day the timer went off right behind me.
The answer is country. Verse 5 says they are coming "…to destroy the whole country." Look at that word "whole," friends. It means the whole land, not a corner of it.

The answer is that the Day of the LORD is near. Verse 6 says, "Wail, for the Day of the LORD is near; it will come as destruction from the Almighty." The cry to wail comes with its reason attached. It's one of the big phrases of this passage, so you'll hear it again.
The answer is melt. Verse 7 says, "…all hands will fall limp, and every man’s heart will melt." It's a picture of fear taking the strength right out of people, friends.

The answer is a woman in labor. Verse 8 says, "Terror, pain, and anguish will seize them; they will writhe like a woman in labor." The picture is pain and fear that grab a person hard. Then the same verse says they will look at one another with faces flushed with fear.

The answer is True. Verse 9 says the Day of the LORD is coming "…to make the earth a desolation and to destroy the sinners within it." That's a hard line, so I won't dress it up, friends. Isaiah says it plainly, and so do I.

The answer is False. Verse 10 says, "The rising sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light." Try finding a light switch in a sky like that, friends. Sun, moon and stars are all dark in this picture.

The answer is the arrogant and the ruthless. Verse 11 says, "I will end the haughtiness of the arrogant and lay low the pride of the ruthless." So the arrogant and the ruthless are the ones brought low, friends.

The answer is that very few people will be left. Verse 12 says, "I will make man scarcer than pure gold, and mankind rarer than the gold of Ophir." Gold is hard to find, so the picture is that people will be hard to find. Not many left, friends.

The answer is people. Verse 14 says, "…each will return to his own people, each will flee to his native land." Everyone heads back toward home, friends. The verse also says they're like a hunted gazelle and a sheep without a shepherd.

The answer is False. Verse 17 says, "Behold, I will stir up against them the Medes, who have no regard for silver and no desire for gold." Imagine a crowd that doesn't care about treasure, friends. That's what the text says about the Medes.

The answer is Sodom and Gomorrah. Verse 19 says Babylon "…will be overthrown by God like Sodom and Gomorrah." Babylon was called the jewel of the kingdoms, and that's the comparison Isaiah reaches for. A big fall for a big name, friends.

The answer is True. Verse 20 says, "She will never be inhabited or settled from generation to generation…" That word "never" is doing heavy lifting, friends. And the next part says no nomad will pitch a tent there and no shepherd will rest a flock there.

The answer is desert creatures and ostriches. Verse 21 says, "But desert creatures will lie down there, and howling creatures will fill her houses. Ostriches will dwell there, and wild goats will leap about." The old houses get a whole different crowd of residents, friends. Verse 22 adds that hyenas will howl in her fortresses and jackals in her luxurious palaces (Isaiah 13:22).
The answer is False. Verse 22 closes with, "Babylon’s time is at hand, and her days will not be prolonged." It's a short, firm last line, friends. No extra years are promised there.
